title: Implement Level Load Analytics Event in Editor
description: The product team for the CloudLedger Engine wants to gather basic usage metrics to understand user behavior within the level editor. The initial requirement is to track every time a user successfully loads a level. This requires integrating with the existing serverless analytics pipeline. The task is broken down into multiple sessions to simulate a typical development workflow of investigation followed by implementation.

project_spec.name: CloudLedger Engine
project_spec.description:
CloudLedger Engine is a serverless-native C game-engine platform designed for enterprise-grade interactive simulations, digital twins, and serious-game training products. While it delivers all the expected real-time features—physics, graphics rendering, AI behaviors, networking, scripting, and an extensible level editor—it is architected primarily to empower businesses to build, distribute, and monetize immersive training, sales-enablement, and data-visualization experiences without maintaining monolithic game servers.  

The engine decomposes traditional runtime responsibilities into stateless micro-services (written in C and compiled for AWS, Azure, or GCP serverless runtimes) that execute on-demand: collision resolution, authoritative state snapshots, analytics ingestion, licensing checks, and save-system persistence. A lightweight client runtime (SDL2 + WebAssembly build) streams resources from S3/Blob Storage, requests simulation ticks through API Gateway/Cloud Functions, and applies delta updates locally via an Entity-Component-System game loop. Because every subsystem—physics, AI, audio mixing, scripting, and input handling—implements publish/subscribe through an Observer Pattern and exposes command queues, teams can hot-patch logic, roll out new business courses, or A/B test UI flows in minutes. Combined with built-in telemetry, CloudLedger Engine turns what was once a pure entertainment toolchain into a scalable, pay-per-use business application platform.
dependencies: AWS Lambda (C Runtime) / Azure Functions for C
AWS API Gateway / Azure API Management
AWS DynamoDB / Azure Cosmos DB (save_system, state_machine persistence)
Amazon S3 / Azure Blob Storage (resource_management, level assets)
Amazon EventBridge / Azure Event Grid (Observer_Pattern message bus)
AWS Step Functions / Durable Functions (command orchestration)
OpenGL ES via ANGLE / WebGL for graphics_rendering
Emscripten (WebAssembly build pipeline for browser delivery)
Terraform / AWS CDK (IaC for serverless deployment)
